title: Bishop and knight: pick the corner, keep the count
outcomes: Reads the bishop's colour and names the pair of corners the mate can be given in, in an unlabeled position
Keeps a won position won by choosing moves that fit inside the fifty-move count
Recognises a position where the corner idea does not apply

steps.text: In *Bishop and knight against a lone king: the right corner* you learned the two phases and the colour rule. Now the positions come without labels. Before the first move run two checks: the **bishop's colour** names the corners you may aim for, and the **halfmove clock** says how much time is left. Keep the win in the next two positions.

**Rule of thumb:** aim for the corner whose colour matches your bishop, and do not spend half-moves you cannot afford. A lone king beside the wrong corner can cost many extra half-moves. With the clock at 60 you have 40 half-moves left. The clock is the same in all three positions below; predict each result.

steps.title: Which corner, with the clock at 60
steps.prompt: White to move, bishop and knight against a lone king, halfmove clock 60 in every position. In the second only the black king has moved; in the third the whole board is reflected left to right. Predict win, draw or loss for each.
Before each position: did you read the bishop's colour and the clock before you chose a plan? Which of the two did you forget more often?
